meta.title: OFF TTRPG — Campaign Bestiary (consolidated, verified)
meta.supersedes: the six per-zone derived files; this is the single canonical enemy database for the campaign
meta.sources: canon merged from off.fandom.com (2008 + remaster) and off.miraheze.org (2025 remake); magnitudes derived from party throughput at anchor levels; verified via coverage audit + prose sweep

zone_identities.Zone 2: Silence. Mute-heavy fodder (Upside-down, Massu, Whale) escalating into Japhet — the library zone takes the party voice away. CP drain continues via Massu.
zone_identities.Zone 3: Vesper fights back: healer adds create kill-order puzzles, hard statuses arrive (Palsy, Furious, double-riders), enemy gauges reach party speed, and the boss drains CP and rewrites elements. The sugar-withdrawal zone makes the party feel the sickness.
zone_identities.The Room: The Room turns the party on itself: Madness, Furious, and Asleep dominate fodder; the Queen fights with her own add-on party as the finale's mirror-foreshadow; the Judge hunts individuals. Psychological zone — control of your own characters is what gets attacked.

notes.fortuna_note: Fortuna roams Zones 1-2 (remake location data); usable as a rare spawn in either.
notes.deferred: Purified-zone content (Secretaries, Source, Maldicion, Psalmanazar & Herodotus, Justus, Carnival) is endgame Grand-collection content, statted last at Room-tier levels (16-20).
notes.model: dpa x gauge-rate x damage-share, x0.85 acc/DEF/element; incoming = frac x heal throughput; calibrated to hand-worked Common Spectre / One-eyed / Dedan examples
notes.composition_note: Canon comps mix freely: Blind + Mute Spectres + Cavalry-burnt + Crown in one fight. Build encounters as strikers + 1 healer; two healers (Crown + Elsen?) is the hard variant.
notes.campaign_sequence: Room (16-18, ends: Judge) -> Purified Zones + superbosses incl. Sugar/Zone 0 (18-20) -> The Batter & Add-Ons (20, campaign finale)

new_enemy_statuses.Thorns: lose 10% max HP each time you act, 2 turns (Source). Anti-fast-class: the inverse of Palsy.
new_enemy_statuses.Famine: Poisoned at double tick, 2/25 max HP (Source).
new_enemy_statuses.Impure: weak to a random ring element, 2 turns (Maldicion, Carnival-Cancer). Interacts with element-change rules; one-instance applies.
new_enemy_statuses.Vilified: prevents Competence use — maps onto the system's Muted, applied party-wide (P&H Vilify). CORRECTED: earlier damage-debuff definition was a guess; Cob's Advent wording proves the remake base effect.
new_enemy_statuses.Defamed: THE CRIT GIFT (canon, corrected): marks one member; guaranteed charged crits for 3 turns; at fade, all damage/healing/statuses that member produced reflect onto the whole party. Curable by Focus. The temptation mechanic — spending the gift is the trap, supporting through it is the answer.

notes.corrosion_note: Alpha's Corrosion (level 18) treats Light immunity as Neutral — it unlocks exactly when the party meets the all-Light-immune Secretaries. Engine and campaign click together.
notes.structure: Secretaries roam all purified zones as elite packs; Source/Maldicion/P&H are the three keys; Justus is the gate; Sugar (Zone 0), Cob (The Room), and Carnival (Infinite Valley) are the optional peaks. Justus and Carnival-Aquarius mirror the party's own kits — the Batter finale's foreshadow.
notes.the_mirror_thesis: Six against four, and the asymmetry is the meaning: the party's Purifier, Alpha, Omega, and Epsilon face their literal canon counterparts — but the Bandit and the Burnt have no mirror. They are this campaign's inventions, the things this world made that the Batter never accounted for. The two classes with no counterpart are the margin the party wins by. Justus foreshadowed it, Carnival rehearsed it, the Queen mourned it: the party has been fighting toward this mirror since Zone 1.
notes.kill_order_final_exam: Omega Add-On first (the cure engine), Epsilon second (the buffed AoE), Alpha third (the locks), the Batter last — or any other order, and the fight teaches why. Every lesson from Crown of the Dead through Ipsilon comes due.
notes.gm_notes: The Batter speaks in Phase 1 — calm, certain, purposeful. He does not speak in Phase 2. Wide Angle on Bad Batter should return garbage or nothing (canon: resists analysis). If the party loses: the world switches off zone by zone. If they win: they choose what the Judge chose. The ending is theirs.

meta.software_ready: all 59 entries carry: element (Sugar for support entities), hp (numeric; compound fights carry units[]), def/res/lck, gauge_s (phase fights carry gauge_phases), status_tiers, and structured moves[] (n/t/mp/acc/fx; acc None = cannot miss, scripted, or pure-status-via-tier-roll, per system doc). MovePower values are multipliers vs the enemy's own Attack scale; exact ATK/ESP splits per move are hand-tuned in software against dmg_per_action.
meta.engine_scope: BINDING SCOPE RULE: every special, moves[], units[], and element_start field in this file is ENGINE-FACING MECHANICS, not GM flavor. The enforcement boundary’s ambiguity-goes-GM-side tiebreaker does NOT apply inside this file — these behaviors are implemented, with the standing rule that scripted lines auto-fire for AI instances and surface as prompts for GM-piloted ones.
meta.enemy_mechanics_vocabulary: Beyond the standard damage/status/stat/element machinery, enemy kits use these flags — define each ONCE, data-driven thereafter: ignore_def (Photographic Blur, Hoax); pct_current_hp damage riders (Fib 7%, Deceptive Inquiry 15%, Red Herring 7%, Rearrangement 40% — execute-proof by construction); action-blocking statuses extend to the Objects button (Corrupted Vilified = Muted + item-lock, same machinery class as Muted blocking Competences); Impure = weakness-overlay status (target takes 2x from a named ring element, 2 turns, reroll on reapplication); Thorns = on-act self-damage 10% max HP, 2 turns; Famine = Poisoned with parameterized tick (2/25); mark = visible no-effect marker with moves that target the marked member (Watch cycle; AI resolves within 2 actions, 50/50 Boon/Ionosphere); hits:N (Double Attack on the surviving liar = hits:2, sharing the Ashley Bat flag); compound units[] with win_condition and unkillable flags and spawn schedules (Pastel heads, Queen royals, Sugar Dummies, the finale) — REQUIRED core machinery, the win-condition inversion is explicit; decoy units vanish when struck and Wide Angle reveals the real one (Gnosticus — rides the reveal-gating system).
meta.sanctioned_custom_features: Exactly TWO mechanisms exceed the vocabulary and are sanctioned as bespoke engine features, fully specified in their entries — implement as written, do not simplify: (1) DEFAMED (P&H): accumulate the marked member’s outputs for 3 of their turns (guaranteed visible charged crits throughout); on expiry, damage dealt hits every party member and heals/buffs cast reflect as party-wide heals/buffs; Focus cures early. (2) CARNIVAL PRIZES: per-Game named condition watched on BOTH sides; any actor meeting it gains an instant 50% gauge fill (Leo: healing / Cancer: elemental attacks / Pisces: being hit / Aquarius: casting any competence). Anything else that seems to need custom code gets flagged to the GM, never half-built.

enemies.name: Japhet
enemies.element_note: GM-assignable: Meat rotates the matchup seesaw — Dedan (Metal) doubled Alpha and halved Smoke classes; Japhet (Meat) doubles Bandit/Omega and halves Alpha
enemies.special: Three forms at 20/35/45% of 5100 HP. CANONICAL ROTATIONS (scripted, per canon — the fight is learnable): Form 1 "Parasite": Warble, Warble, Alto (repeat). Form 2 "Master": Warble, Alto, Warble, Soprano. Form 3 "Firebird": Soprano, Alto, Head-Voice, Warble, Tenor. Moves: Warble 1.1x Meat acc 95 | Alto 0.8x + Muted acc 90 | Soprano 1.5x Esp acc 92 | Head-Voice 2.2x acc 90 | Tenor 1.0x + Poisoned acc 90. SUMMONS (canon: "he attempts to summon various spectres"): each form transition summons 2 Upside-down Spectres at Zone 2 stats — the adds arrive exactly when his gauge quickens, and they carry Mute too. This is his real action economy; the party's AoE (Long String, Absolute Tragedy, fresh at 9-10) is the intended answer. Pressure model: direct ~18/s in form 3 + Poison ticks on afflicted members (~2/s each) + Mute landing on Purifier/Omega deleting heal throughput — the three stack to ~0.9x heal capacity without needing Hasty or adds. Mute on Omega/Burnt disables their kits — stock cure items; Focus cannot self-cure a Muted Omega. Statuses: Strong immune Palsied/Asleep/Muted/Madness; Light immune Blinded/Furious/Poisoned; stat changes land.

enemies.special: The element storm — the Burnt's final exam. IMPURE (new status, remake): target becomes weak to a random ring element, 2 turns. Entropic Piety: self-hit 0.8x + rerolls his OWN Impure weakness. Unstable Purity: 1.4x single + Impure on the target. Clamor Claws: full-party 1.0x in WHATEVER ELEMENT HE IS CURRENTLY WEAK TO — tracking his weakness tells you the incoming element, and Sable Rush (set party element to resist it) is the designed answer. Wide Angle reads his current weakness: the 2 CP scout competence becomes boss-critical. Wants: element tracking, Sable Rush timing, exploit windows. Sweet Madness keeps the Burnt unshiftable.

enemies.name: Psalmanazar & Herodotus
enemies.element_note: GM-assignable: liars and smoke
enemies.special: The liars' duo — two bodies, one fight, natural action economy. Shared kit (canon): VILIFY: whole party rolls Vilified = Muted (competence lock). SUBTERFUGE: marks ONE party member with DEFAMED — THE CRIT GIFT: for 3 of their turns the marked member rolls a charged crit on EVERY gauge fill (visibly glowing, every time). When Defamed fades, everything they did during the window reflects onto the entire party: accumulated damage dealt hits every party member; healing and buffs cast reflect as healing and buffs to everyone. The trap is the temptation — a striker who spends three guaranteed crits attacking deals ~350-450 to each party member at the fade (a wipe); a marked member who heals, buffs, or Defends turns the lie into a blessing. Focus can cure Defamed early — stripping your own guaranteed crits, the cure that feels bad to use. FIB: 1.0x + 7% of target current HP. DECEPTIVE INQUIRY: 1.2x + 15% current HP — execute-proof strikes. FACADE: spawns THREE Gnosticus (shell game, per canon: only ONE is real — 280 HP, casts Red Herring at 1.0x + 7% current HP; the two fakes vanish when struck, the wasted action being the point. Wide Angle reveals the real one: the 2 CP scout earns its keep against liars). When one brother dies the survivor gains Double Attack permanently. The whole fight is epistemology: what is real, what is a gift, what is a lie. Statuses: superboss template; stat changes land.

enemies.name: Sugar (+4 Dummies)
enemies.element_note: the ONLY Sugar-element entity: no weakness, no resistance, exactly as the ring promises — elements simply do not help here
enemies.special: The status hurricane at machine-gun speed — fastest entity in the campaign (canon AGL 250 both her and the Dummies). Kit (canon 2008 weights + remake statuses, Confused=Madness per GM ruling): Quatre-Quarts 1.9x heavy + Madness | Caramel Dur 1.2x + Palsied | Mille-Feuilles: ATK Down 25% + Furious | Dame Blanche: cheap pure Madness (no damage, no accuracy roll) | Parfait au Chocolat: all-party 1.1x. The DUMMIES are the fight: 60 HP each but acting every 1.6s — Sick Mask heals Sugar ~130, Empathetic Mask gives her DEF Up +20, and BLIND MASK GRANTS SUGAR HASTY (remake, canon-sanctioned enemy-side Hasty). Four dummies die to four attacks — but every gauge spent killing one is a gauge Sugar spends casting Madness. Elements dead, statuses everywhere: this is the anti-Carnival — the fight where half the party's tech does not apply.

enemies.name: Carnival
enemies.element_note: takes the element theme of whichever Game is active (Leo Meat / Cancer Impure-rotating / Pisces Smoke / Aquarius Plastic)
enemies.special: THE CAPSTONE RAID, ~290s at 13600 HP: four Games at 25% HP each, cycling Leo -> Cancer -> Pisces -> Aquarius, each borrowing a superboss kit the party has already beaten (canon: 13 competences). LEO (Source): Flourish self-heal + Swan Dive Palsy. CANCER (Maldicion): Clamor Claws + Unstable Purity with Impure. PISCES (P&H): Red Herring (+7% current HP) + HOAX: all-party, ignores DEF. AQUARIUS (Justus): Surrealist Tragedy, Requisite Bracket, and ULTIMATE HOMERUN — the Purifier's own capstone, 2.6x + Madness, cast at the party. PRIZES (remake mechanic, canon-corrected): BIDIRECTIONAL TEMPO WAR. Each Game names a condition — Leo: using healing / Cancer: using elemental attacks / Pisces: being hit / Aquarius: using any competence — and EITHER SIDE that meets it wins a prize: the winner's current gauge instantly fills 50%. The conditions apply to Carnival too: in Leo his Flourish self-heals win HIM prizes (healing accelerates him), in Pisces every hit the party takes accelerates them (getting hurt is tempo), in Aquarius every competence anyone casts accelerates its caster — a fight where the rules of speed change every phase and the party must play each Game's condition harder than Carnival does. Carnival is the final exam on every mechanic the endgame taught, and Aquarius firing the party's own ultimate back is the last note before the Batter does it for real.

enemies.name: Cob
enemies.element_note: GM-assignable: auroras and ionosphere — sky-stuff is Smoke
enemies.special: THE CAPRICIOUS GOD (Aries to Carnival's Sagittarius). Tankiest superboss: DEF 35 (remake 78, highest in the game) and fast (2.0s). THE WATCH CYCLE: every ~25s, WATCH WITH GREAT INTEREST marks a random party member (visible, no effect). Within his next two actions he resolves it as either GRANT A BOON — heals the watched member 75% of current HP, a genuine gift — or IONOSPHERE: 9999 to the watched member. Unconditional death; no mitigation survives it. The answers are Sacred Mission (once), a ready revive, or accepting the loss — the fight is revive-economy management against a god who sometimes blesses instead. Roughly 50/50, never telegraphed which. RESHUFFLE PRESSURE: Rearrangement of Solid Objects — all-party 0.8x + 40% of each target's CURRENT HP (execute-proof, softens everyone before the next judgment). CONJUGATE AURORAS: self-heal 1160 (13.5% max) as an action — the DPS-check component. ADVENT OF THE CORRUPTED ERA (once per fight, below 50% HP): whole party rolls Corrupted Vilified — Muted AND item-locked, 2 turns. In this economy that is the scariest debuff possible: no competences, no items, no revives — Attack and Defend only while the judgment cycle keeps running. Statuses: superboss template; stat changes land (DEF shred is the honest tech against DEF 35).

enemies.special: THE MIRROR. His kit IS the Purifier class kit at boss scale — the system's own provenance made flesh: Furious Homerun 2.1x Sugar | Special Homerun 2.9x Sugar | ULTIMATE HOMERUN 3.8x Sugar (~every 40s, telegraphed one gauge ahead) | the four ELEMENTAL RUNS — he reads the party and casts the Run that doubles against his chosen target: element chess played back at them | Save Second Base — heals an Add-On ~150 (his healing keeps HIS party alive; kill-order pressure) | Wide Angle, cosmetically, because he is scouting them. SACRED MISSION (his level-2 passive) IS THE PHASE TRANSITION: the first lethal blow leaves him at 1 HP. He stands. He speaks his line. And then the party sees what the Judge saw.

enemies.special: THE BEAST, ~150s. Phase 1 was chess; phase 2 is violence. No heals, no allies, no element games — the fastest sustained gauge of any final entity (1.9s) with visible charged crits at LCK 12. Kit: DEAD AIM 2.4x single | SANCTIFY: all-party 1.2x SUGAR (purification turned on the party — unresistable by design, the one Sugar-damage enemy in the campaign besides its old self) | SILENCE: all-party Muted roll, the switch motif made mechanical | PURIFICATION retained: +25% vs players below 30% — wounded players are prey, triage is survival | Ultimate Homerun, still, because the swing never changed. By now the party's items and CP are the campaign's last reserves: this phase is the economy document's final exam. Statuses: Strong immune to everything hard, Light immune to the rest — but stat changes STILL LAND, because they always do. The Burnt cannot change its element (Sweet Madness) and the beast cannot change what it is. Fitting.
